data.title: Merz calls for unity as he warns of threats facing Germany
data.description:
Key points:
  • Merz urges unity amid coalition strains after election setbacks
  • Warns of extremism, accuses Russia of destabilisation
  • Urges economic reforms, rejects cooperation with far-right AfD

Chancellor Friedrich Merz called for unity in his struggling coalition on Saturday, saying Germany faced growing threats from political extremists and what he described as daily Russian efforts to destabilise the country.

Speaking at a conference of the Christian Social Union (CSU), the Bavarian sister party of his conservative Christian Democrats (CDU), Merz said Germany faced "extraordinarily serious challenges".

"How do we safeguard our freedom and our security in Europe, in the face of growing threats from extremists within and foreign powers from without?" he said, adding that Russia was seeking "to destabilise Germany on a daily basis".

Relations between Berlin and Moscow have fallen to their lowest level since the Cold War following Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine but Russia rejects accusations that it is conducting a hybrid campaign against Germany and other European countries.

Merz's comments follow weeks of tension with the ruling coalition after heavy regional election defeats in eastern Germany, where the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) came first in two states and the far-left Left Party topped the poll in Berlin.

Merz's approval ratings have fallen to record lows, while tensions have surfaced both between the coalition partners and between the CDU and CSU.

The two conservative sister parties have a long history of disagreements but have generally managed to overcome them.

On Saturday, delegates broke into loud applause when Merz mentioned Ilse Aigner, the CSU politician the party has proposed as successor to German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, who is due to step down next year.

The CDU has so far stopped short of endorsing Aigner, and party sources say it has not abandoned hopes of putting forward its own candidate for the largely ceremonial post of head of state.

Merz, who entered the conference hall to a Bavarian brass band playing "The Eye of the Tiger", praised CSU ministers in the government and paid tribute to CSU leader Markus Soeder.

But he repeated his rejection of calls from some conservatives to seek ways of cooperating with the AfD, which leads national opinion polls, saying any politician who voted with the party "has no place in our Union".

He also urged the Social Democrats (SPD) and Greens not to form a coalition in Berlin with the Left Party, which he accused of tolerating antisemitism within its ranks. The Left Party denies any systemic antisemitism in the party.

Merz said rapid reforms to Germany's pension, tax and welfare systems were essential to revive the economy and restore confidence in public institutions.

data.title: ESMO 2026: NUBEQA® (darolutamide) Plus ADT and Radiation Therapy Reduces Risk of Metastasis or Death by 58% in Prostate Cancer Patients at High Risk of Recurrence
data.description:
New late-breaking data to be presented today by the Australian and New Zealand Urogenital and Prostate (ANZUP) Clinical Trials Group at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 will show that adding Bayer’s androgen receptor inhibitor (ARi), NUBEQA® (darolutamide), to standard-of-care androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and locoregional radiation therapy (RT), improves metastasis-free survival based on conventional imaging (MFS-CI) in prostate cancer patients with high risk of recurrence compared to placebo. These data will be presented at Presidential Symposium I at the ESMO Congress 2026 (LBA4, Saturday, October 24, at 16:30 CEST/10:30 am ET).

NUBEQA is indicated in the U.S. for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC) both with and without docetaxel, and for the treatment of adult patients with non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (nmCRPC).1

At a median follow-up of 3.8 years, the interim analysis demonstrated a statistically significant 58% reduction in the risk of metastasis or death with NUBEQA plus ADT and RT compared with placebo plus ADT and RT (hazard ratio [HR] 0.42; 95% CI: 0.27–0.66; p=0.0001).2 The 4-year metastasis-free survival rate was 95% for patients receiving NUBEQA compared with 88% for those receiving placebo.2

“Prostate cancer patients at a high risk of relapse face a considerable risk of recurrence and metastatic spread, making early, effective intervention vital,” said Dr. Tamim Niazi, Associate Professor of Oncology at McGill University, Radiation Oncologist at the Jewish General Hospital in Montreal, Canada, and Co-Lead Investigator of the study. “The improvement in metastasis-free survival seen in interim results from the DASL-HiCaP trial highlights the potential of adding darolutamide to standard androgen deprivation therapy and radiation therapy to help prevent or delay disease progression in patients who are at high risk of progression despite receiving primary curative therapy.”

Secondary endpoints showed NUBEQA was associated with a 53% reduction in the risk of prostate-specific antigen progression or death (PSA-PFS; HR 0.47; 95% CI: 0.33–0.67), and a 4-year PSA-PFS rate of 91% versus 83% with placebo.2 Prostate cancer-specific survival (PCSS) and overall survival (OS) hazard ratios were 0.58 (95% CI: 0.17–1.97; 99% vs 99% at 4 years) and 0.88 (95% CI: 0.49–1.59; 97% vs 95% at 4 years), respectively, with follow-up ongoing.2

The safety profile of NUBEQA was consistent with previous studies. The proportions of patients experiencing Grade ≥2 adverse events of special interest for NUBEQA versus placebo were: fatigue/asthenia (14% vs 10%), hypertension (7% vs 9%), fractures (2% vs 3%), and cardiac events (3% vs 3%). Any Grade ≥3 adverse event occurred in 43% of patients in the NUBEQA group versus 36% in the placebo group.2

“These new data underscore the potential of darolutamide to improve outcomes for patients in the early prostate cancer setting, adding to the broad body of evidence helping to support its use across different stages of the disease,” said Christine Roth, Executive Vice President, Global Product Strategy and Commercialization at Bayer’s Pharmaceuticals Division. “Bayer is proud to support research by ANZUP, the Sydney Clinical Trials Centre, Canadian Cancer Trials Group, and international partners, for men with prostate cancer.”

About the DASL-HiCaP trial (ANZUP1801)

The DASL-HiCaP trial is an investigator-initiated, randomized, placebo-controlled, Phase III trial (NCT04136353) evaluating NUBEQA added to standard-of-care ADT and locoregional radiation therapy in prostate cancer patients at high risk of recurrence.

DASL-HiCaP was conducted in collaboration with the University of Sydney and ANZUP Clinical Trials Group and is the fourth Phase III trial for darolutamide to be presented at a prestigious international conference.

A total of 1,106 participants across Australia, New Zealand, Canada, the United States, Ireland and the United Kingdom were randomized 1:1 to receive NUBEQA (600 mg twice daily) or matching placebo for 96 weeks, combined with an LHRH analog for 96 weeks and RT to the prostate/prostate bed and pelvic lymph nodes.

The primary endpoint was metastasis-free survival based on conventional imaging (MFS-CI). Secondary endpoints included prostate-specific antigen progression free survival (PSA-PFS), prostate cancer-specific survival (PCSS), and overall survival (OS). The protocol specified an interim analysis after 87 MFS-CI events; follow-up is ongoing to evaluate long-term overall survival.

About NUBEQA® (darolutamide)1

NUBEQA® (darolutamide) is an androgen receptor inhibitor (ARi) with a distinct chemical structure that competitively inhibits androgen binding, AR nuclear translocation, and AR-mediated transcription.

NUBEQA was developed jointly by Bayer and Orion Corporation, a globally operating Finnish pharmaceutical company.

NUBEQA is an androgen receptor inhibitor indicated for the treatment of adult patients with:

  • Non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (nmCRPC)

  • Metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC)

  • Metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC) in combination with docetaxel

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

Warnings & Precautions

Ischemic Heart Disease – Ischemic heart disease, including fatal cases, occurred in patients receiving NUBEQA.

In a pooled analysis of ARAMIS and ARANOTE, ischemic heart disease occurred in 3.4% of patients receiving NUBEQA and 2.2% receiving placebo, including Grade 3-4 events in 1.4% and 0.3%, respectively. Ischemic events led to death in 0.4% of patients receiving NUBEQA and 0.4% receiving placebo.

In ARASENS, ischemic heart disease occurred in 3.2% of patients receiving NUBEQA with docetaxel and 2% receiving placebo with docetaxel, including Grade 3-4 events in 1.3% and 1.1%, respectively. Ischemic events led to death in 0.3% of patients receiving NUBEQA with docetaxel and 0% receiving placebo with docetaxel.

Monitor for signs and symptoms of ischemic heart disease. Optimize management of cardiovascular risk factors, such as hypertension, diabetes, or dyslipidemia. Discontinue NUBEQA for Grade 3-4 ischemic heart disease.

Seizure – Seizure occurred in patients receiving NUBEQA.

In a pooled analysis of ARAMIS and ARANOTE, Grade 1-3 seizure occurred in 0.2% of patients receiving NUBEQA. Seizure occurred from 261 to 665 days after initiation of NUBEQA.

In ARASENS, seizure occurred in 0.8% of patients receiving NUBEQA with docetaxel, including two Grade 3 events. Seizure occurred from 38 to 1754 days after initiation of NUBEQA.

It is unknown whether anti-epileptic medications will prevent seizures with NUBEQA. Advise patients of the risk of developing a seizure while receiving NUBEQA and of engaging in any activity where sudden loss of consciousness could cause harm to themselves or others. Consider discontinuation of NUBEQA in patients who develop a seizure during treatment.

Embryo-Fetal Toxicity – The safety and efficacy of NUBEQA have not been established in females. NUBEQA can cause fetal harm and loss of pregnancy. Advise males with female partners of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment with NUBEQA and for 1 week after the last dose.

Adverse Reactions

In ARAMIS, serious adverse reactions occurred in 25% of patients receiving NUBEQA and in 20% of patients receiving placebo. Serious adverse reactions in ≥1% of patients who received NUBEQA included urinary retention, pneumonia, and hematuria. Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 3.9% of patients receiving NUBEQA and 3.2% of patients receiving placebo. Fatal adverse reactions that occurred in ≥2 patients who received NUBEQA included death (0.4%), cardiac failure (0.3%), cardiac arrest (0.2%), general physical health deterioration (0.2%), and pulmonary embolism (0.2%). The most common (>2% with a ≥2% increase compared to placebo) adverse reactions, including laboratory test abnormalities, were increased AST (23%), decreased neutrophil count (20%), fatigue (16%), increased bilirubin (16%), pain in extremity (6%), and rash (4%). Clinically relevant adverse reactions occurring in 2% or more of patients treated with NUBEQA included ischemic heart disease (4%) and heart failure (2.1%).

In ARANOTE, serious adverse reactions occurred in 24% of patients receiving NUBEQA. Serious adverse reactions in ≥1% of patients who received NUBEQA included pneumonia (2%), urinary tract infection (1.8%), musculoskeletal pain (1.6%), hemorrhage (1.6%), arrhythmias (1.3%), and spinal cord compression (1.1%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 4.7% of patients receiving NUBEQA and those that occurred in ≥2 patients included sepsis (1.1%), craniocerebral injury (0.4%), and myocardial infarction (0.4%). The most common (≥10% with a ≥2% increase compared to placebo) adverse reaction is urinary tract infection (12%). The most common laboratory test abnormalities (≥15% with a ≥5% increase over placebo) are increased AST (32%), increased ALT (28%), increased bilirubin (17%), and decreased neutrophil count (16%). Clinically relevant adverse reactions in <10% of patients who received NUBEQA included arrhythmia (8.8%), pneumonia (3.6%), and myocardial infarction (0.7%).

In ARASENS, serious adverse reactions occurred in 45% of patients receiving NUBEQA with docetaxel. Serious adverse reactions in ≥2% of patients who received NUBEQA with docetaxel included febrile neutropenia (6%), neutrophil count decreased (2.8%), musculoskeletal pain (2.6%) and pneumonia (2.6%). Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 4% of patients receiving NUBEQA with docetaxel. Fatal adverse reactions in ≥2 patients who received NUBEQA included COVID-19/COVID-19 pneumonia (0.8%), myocardial infarction (0.3%), and sudden death (0.3%). The most common (≥10% with a ≥2% increase over placebo with docetaxel) adverse reactions are constipation (23%), rash (20%), decreased appetite (19%), hemorrhage (18%), increased weight (18%), and hypertension (14%). The most common laboratory test abnormalities (≥30%) are anemia (72%), hyperglycemia (57%), decreased lymphocyte count (52%), decreased neutrophil count (49%), increased AST (40%), increased ALT (37%), and hypocalcemia (31%). Clinically relevant adverse reactions in <10% of patients who received NUBEQA with docetaxel included fractures (8%), ischemic heart disease (3.2%), seizures (0.6%), and drug-induced liver injury (0.3%).

Drug Interactions

Effect of Other Drugs on NUBEQA – Concomitant use of NUBEQA with a combined P-gp and strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducer decreases darolutamide exposure which may decrease NUBEQA activity. Avoid concomitant use of NUBEQA with combined P-gp and strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers.

Concomitant use of NUBEQA with a combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitor increases darolutamide exposure which may increase the risk of NUBEQA adverse reactions. Monitor patients more frequently for NUBEQA adverse reactions and modify NUBEQA dosage as needed.

Effects of NUBEQA on Other Drugs – NUBEQA is an inhibitor of BCRP transporter. Concomitant use of NUBEQA increases the AUC and Cmax of BCRP substrates, which may increase the risk of BCRP substrate-related toxicities. Avoid concomitant use with drugs that are BCRP substrates where possible. If used together, monitor patients more frequently for adverse reactions, and consider dose reduction of the BCRP substrate drug.

NUBEQA is an inhibitor of OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters. Concomitant use of NUBEQA may increase the plasma concentrations of OATP1B1 or OATP1B3 substrates. Monitor patients more frequently for adverse reactions of these drugs and consider dose reduction while patients are taking NUBEQA.

Review the Prescribing Information of drugs that are BCRP, OATP1B1, and OATP1B3 substrates when used concomitantly with NUBEQA.

For important risk and use information about NUBEQA, please see the accompanying full Prescribing Information.

Please see the full Prescribing Information.

data.title: Defensive Plays Are Gaining Steam. 5 Heavily Shorted Names Could Pop. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Evie Liu

Some of the market's most beaten-down consumer stocks have been making a comeback — and investors betting against them could provide additional fuel for the rally.

Consumer-staples stocks surged in October as investors shifted money away from technology companies amid concerns about lofty valuations and slowing economic growth. The Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR exchange-traded fund has gained nearly 10% as of Friday's close, reversing a 4.5% decline in September.

Several rebounding companies have seen unusually high short interest. Short sellers borrow and sell shares, hoping to buy them back later at lower prices and pocket the difference. But when a heavily-shorted stock rises sharply, those investors can face mounting losses and may rush to buy shares to close their positions — which could add to demand and push prices even higher.

Flowers Foods, the maker of Nature's Own and Dave's Killer Bread, is one potential candidate. As of Sept. 30, nearly 23% of its publicly traded shares were sold short, according to FactSet. The stock has gained nearly 11% in October through Friday.

Boston Beer, the maker of Samuel Adams and Twisted Tea, also stands out. About 21% of its float was sold short at September's end. Shares have rallied 23% this month through Friday.

There are reasons for caution: Both companies are struggling with declining revenue, raising doubts about whether their stock rallies can last.

In the latest quarter, Flowers Foods reported a 4% revenue decline year over year and lowered its annual earnings forecast. Likewise, Boston Beer's revenue fell 3.2% as its sales volume shrunk nearly 5% from a year ago.

Pet food company Freshpet might be a better bet. Its revenue grew 15.5% year over year in the latest quarter, driven almost entirely by higher sales volumes as the company attracted more customers and expanded distribution.

Still, 17% of its publicly traded shares were sold short by the end of September as investors worried about slowing growth and intensifying competition. Its shares have climbed 11% this month through Friday, potentially putting pressure on short sellers to close their positions if the rally continues.

Freshpet has a days-to-cover ratio — days needed to buy back all the shares sold short at a stock's average daily trading volume — of 7.9 days, compared with 5.3 for Flowers Foods and 5.1 for Boston Beer. That suggests short sellers could face greater difficulty exiting their positions quickly if Freshpet shares surge.

Sprouts Farmers Market and Vital Farms also have relatively high short interest, with about 14% and 24% of their respective floats sold short by the end of September. Both stocks rallied Thursday, although they have been largely flat compared with the beginning of the month.

High short interest, however, doesn't guarantee a squeeze. Some bearish bets reflect genuine business challenges, and short sellers may be willing to withstand temporary losses.

And the defensive rally itself remains fragile. The consumer-staples ETF fell about 2% on Friday, reversing part of its sharp advance on Thursday. Flowers Foods and Freshpet each dropped more than 4%, while Sprouts Farmers Market fell 3.8% and Vital Farms lost 2.9%. Boston Beer bucked the trend, gaining 3.6% following its earnings report on Thursday.

Without sustained buying pressure, short sellers have less incentive to exit. Investors will get another clue on Monday, when updated short-interest figures from Finra become available. The report will show positions as of Oct. 15, revealing whether bearish investors reduced their bets during the staples rally — or continued adding to them.

data.title: Bitcoin Core Speeds Up Bug Fixes As AI Changes Disclosure Rules
data.description:
TL;DR: Bitcoin Core has adopted faster fixes and disclosure for vulnerabilities that are easy to rediscover, including with AI. Longer embargoes remain available for other security flaws.

Bitcoin Core is changing the timetable for dealing with security flaws that an attacker can uncover with little effort. The practical question is whether waiting to explain a bug still protects users when software can rediscover it almost immediately.

A policy update merged on October 22 creates a faster route for these cases. Developer Antoine Poinsot argued that large language models have made some problems easier to find, including by identifying fixes that were intended to attract little attention.

That creates a difficult choice for the people maintaining Bitcoin software: withholding details can buy upgrade time, but delaying a usable patch can also leave operators exposed.

Faster Releases For Easily Rediscovered Flaws

The updated disclosure policy allows developers to classify a reported vulnerability as easily discoverable. A simple AI prompt is one example; the category also covers problems found with minimal effort through other means.

For those vulnerabilities, maintainers plan to issue a fix for each supported major version as soon as possible, accompanied by a security advisory. These cases bypass the usual embargo linked to severity.

The distinction matters for an exchange or payment business running its own node. A point release can deliver a targeted repair without waiting for the next major software version. An advisory also helps the operator judge whether its particular configuration is affected.

Other disclosure rules remain. Low-severity issues normally become public two weeks after a major release containing the fix. Medium- and high-severity issues generally wait until two weeks after the last affected version reaches the end of its support life. Critical vulnerabilities still require individual handling.

Less Secrecy Also Means Less Testing Time

The discussion accompanying the change makes clear that speed has a cost. Poinsot noted that accelerated mitigations will spend less time in development branches before reaching users. Developers therefore have to weigh the risk of exposing a flaw against the risk of introducing a faulty repair.

For businesses providing custody, the operational lesson is that patch readiness belongs alongside key security. Maintaining a current inventory of software versions, understanding which services depend on them and having a controlled upgrade process can make a short notice period easier to manage.

The announcement itself does not identify a new attack on the Bitcoin network. It changes how a defined category of software problem will be handled. Readers should therefore distinguish a revised security process from evidence that coins have been stolen or consensus rules have failed.

Its significance is narrower and more practical: when attackers can cheaply rediscover a weakness, keeping users on unfixed software becomes harder to justify. The response shifts toward getting a repair into their hands sooner, while making the remaining trade-offs visible.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: AI fever ignites a boom in thematic ETFs as fund managers hunt for their next big hit
data.description:
By Christine Idzelis

It's been a rocky October for the AI trade, putting a dent in big gains so far this year

Robotics ETFs are increasingly coming to the stock market, with AI being a dominant investing theme in 2026.

The runaway success of the artificial-intelligence trade has left investors hungry for the next big market theme. Wall Street fund managers are happily obliging with a flurry of new targeted products, helping investors invest in everything from the rise of robotics to the incipient space economy.

Thematic ETFs are booming in 2026, as asset managers have launched new products at a breakneck pace. The popularity of funds like the Roundhill Memory ETF DRAM, which invests in memory stocks as a subsector of technology and quickly gained traction because they're an important part of the AI trade, has inspired something of a gold rush in the space, as fund companies cast about for the next big hit.

Niche subdivisions of the AI theme have proved particularly popular, as fund managers have launched products tied to everything from AI lab ecosystems to shares of optical companies expected to benefit from the ongoing AI investment boom. Cybersecurity, robotics and defense have been other popular themes.

"AI is the dominant theme," said Bryan Armour, director of ETF and semiliquid fund research at Morningstar, in a phone interview. "What we're seeing in 2026 is product development that refines some of those exposures," he said, from AI Labs to robotics including humanoids.

So far, 73 thematic ETFs have launched this year in the U.S., an 87% increase from the 39 launches seen in 2025, according to data from Morningstar. But the boom in new products is also dredging up some uncomfortable memories: The previous peak for thematic ETF launches arrived in 2021, as the COVID-era market mania was reaching its crescendo.

 
Thematic ETF launches are surging in 2026 
Year                                          Launches 
2020                                          49 
2021                                          90 
2022                                          59 
2023                                          40 
2024                                          25 
2025                                          39 
2026                                          73 
Source: Morningstar data as of Oct. 19, 2026

While broad index funds like the State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF SPY continue to dominate the league tables of products with the most assets under management, the growth in the thematic space suggests investors are increasingly fixating on a more specific opportunity set.

Over the past couple of years, AI has become more influential as an economic force. Economists now say aggressive investment in new data centers is largely responsible for a pickup in the pace of GDP growth.

"This is one of the biggest themes in a generation," said Jay Jacobs, U.S. head of equity ETFs at BlackRock, in a phone interview. "If you look at what's driving the markets, AI is up there with GDP growth and interest rates as one of the biggest factors."

BlackRock listed on Wednesday the iShares Future Robotics and Related Technologies Active ETF RBTX, which actively invests in stocks in categories such as humanoids, industrial automatization, autonomous vehicles, and space and defense, according to Jacobs.

"This is really looking out at what the next major development could look like in the artificial-intelligence space," he said. "The next phase is really AI entering the physical world."

It's hardly the first robotics-focused product to launch this year. Indeed, it has been a particularly popular theme, according to Aniket Ullal, head of ETF research and analytics at CFRA Research. A handful of products have launched in recent months, including the Tuttle-Rareview Humanoid Robotics ETF HOID, which began trading earlier this month.

"People are trying to disaggregate the AI theme," Ullal told MarketWatch by phone.

AI labs, space, cybersecurity

A bunch of AI-lab ETFs recently arrived to the market, including one centered around OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT, which had helped popularize artificial intelligence after it was introduced to the public in late 2022.

Harbor Capital Advisors launched the OpenAI Lab Ecosystem ETF OAIW in August, along with the Anthropic AI Lab Ecosystem ETF ANTW, Meta AI Lab Ecosystem ETF MTAW, the Google DeepMind AI Lab Ecosystem ETF DEPW and SpaceXAI Lab Ecosystem ETF XAIW.

"The ecosystem is built around these frontier-model developers," said Armour. "They're like company-specific AI labs," with the ETFs holding shares of their partners or backers, he said.

As AI is maturing, many investors want to trade more precisely around the winners and losers as they shake out, according to Matthew Tuttle, CEO of Tuttle Capital Management.

For example, he pointed to the Roundhill Memory ETF, which launched in early April, as "a perfect product at the perfect time," during a phone interview with MarketWatch. The fund was the first ETF to focus on high-bandwidth memory stocks, providing exposure to the "biggest of the bottleneck trades" in AI, including shares of South Korean companies that U.S. investors couldn't easily buy at the time, he said. "Now what you're seeing, everyone is trying to come up with the next DRAM," said Tuttle, referring to the ETF's ticker.

Since then, he has launched other products offering exposure to the ongoing data-center buildout. In May, his firm launched the Tuttle Capital Pure Play Photonics ETF FOTO, which provides exposure to stocks involved in using laser light in optical fiber instead of copper wire for AI data centers. That same month saw the listing of the Corgi Lithography & Semiconductor Photonics ETF EUV, which Morningstar categorizes under the AI and Big Data theme.

Corgi has launched a flurry of ETF products this year, including a number of thematic funds, like the Corgi Robots & Humanoids ETF CBOT, Corgi Space & Satellite Communications ETF DIPR, Corgi Data & Surveillance ETF EYES, and Corgi AI Cybersecurity ETF XA, according to Morningstar data. Space, another popular theme, has been supercharged by the IPO of Elon Musk's SpaceX in June.

Cybersecurity has also been a big theme, as frontier AI models have seen their capabilities quickly advance. A few high-profile incidents where autonomous AI agents broke out of their sandboxes and infiltrated third-party systems have helped to underscore its importance.

The First Trust Nasdaq Cybersecurity ETF CIBR, which launched in 2015, is currently the biggest cybersecurity product in ETF land. It had $17 billion under management at the end of September, according to Morningstar data.

The AI trade's volatile October

It's been a rocky October for the AI trade as investors question the return on investment from companies doing a heavy amount of spending and borrowing relating to AI to support the buildout of the technology's infrastructure. Still, AI-related stocks have broadly seen big 2026 gains.

Among ETFs that invest in the broad theme, the iShares A. I. Innovation and Tech Active ETF BAI is up more than 21% in 2026 despite tumbling more than 14% this month through Friday. Similarly, the Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF AIQ has jumped more than 22% so far this year, although the fund had a much smaller October loss, of more than 4% through Friday, according to FactSet data.

AI is attracting heightened focus lately, after SpaceX (SPCX) reported third-quarter earnings on Oct. 20, and Facebook parent Meta Platforms (META) and Tesla (TSLA) each released quarterly results the following day. Next week brings highly anticipated results from other Big Tech companies involved in AI, including Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL) (GOOG).

With investors now getting access to many different funds with more precise exposures to AI, it's important to remember amid excitement over the transformative technology that "price matters" when identifying investing opportunities in the stock market, Armour cautioned.

"There's so much projection in valuing AI companies," he said, "that it makes it really hard to know whether you're still coming in before the full wave or if you're buying in on the crest."

Bull market for stocks

That S&P 500's strong run in 2026 and in each of the past three years appears to have set the stage for this year's jump in thematic ETFs, as investors sift through ways to sharpen their investing approach in the current bull market for U.S. stocks. The previous thematic ETF boom in 2021 - which Armour said was fueled in part by strategies around environmental, social and governance criteria known as ESG that included clean energy - also coincided with a strong bull market.

In 2021, the S&P 500 SPX booked its third consecutive year of double-digit percentage gains, before slumping 19.4% in 2022 to book its worst performance since 2008, according to FactSet data. The pace of thematic ETF launches fell off significantly in 2022.

AI has been a significant tailwind for the market this year, despite some concern over higher financing costs following a jump in bond yields and as many investors expect the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates again by year's end. The Fed had been raising rates aggressively in 2022, the year the U.S. stock market slumped, in an effort to battle soaring inflation.

Today, inflation remains elevated, albeit well below levels seen in 2022, prompting the Fed to hike its policy rate in September. The S&P 500 has climbed 11.4% this year through Friday, ending 2.5% below its record closing high booked Oct. 6, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

"When the stock market is particularly strong, then thematic funds tend to follow," said Armour. "When everything seems to be working, it's a lot easier to take on risk."

-Christine Idzelis

data.title: Cordelia Cruises launches Cordelia Sky, expands fleet to two ships
data.description:
Mumbai-headquartered Cordelia Cruises has launched Cordelia Sky, its largest cruise vessel, and commenced commercial sailings on Friday, October 23, 2026. The launch event was attended by representatives from the media and tourism industry.

The launch marks the company’s transition from a single-ship operator to a two-ship fleet operator. Its next vessel, Cordelia Sun, is scheduled to be launched in 2027.

Company targets global cruise market growth

Addressing the media at the launch, Cordelia Cruises President and CEO Jurgen Bailom said the company had carried more than eight lakh passengers since commencing operations. He said the company was founded with a vision of making cruising a preferred travel option for Indians.

“Our goal is, by 2032, to be the top five largest cruise market in the world,” Bailom said.

The company, a subsidiary of Waterways Leisure Tourism Ltd, also plans to create 20,000 additional jobs over the next three years. As part of its workforce development initiatives, Cordelia Cruises has started a cadet programme and is moving closer to having its first female captain.

Bailom also mentioned about the launch of The Chairman’s Club, a loyalty programme rewarding members.

Looking ahead, the company has planned a 34-day cruise from Mumbai to Sydney during the 2028 monsoon season. The itinerary is expected to cover seven countries and 16 ports.

Geopolitical developments pose cost challenges

Commenting on the impact of geopolitical developments on the cruise business, Bailom highlighted the rising costs of food and fuel.

“However, we are still able to manage. But it can’t get worse than it is right now, so we all hope that everything is going to get better soon,” he said.

A 12-deck vessel with over 1,000 cabins

Measuring approximately 260 metres in length (848 feet approximately), Cordelia Sky spans 12 decks and has a gross tonnage of 77,104. The vessel has 1,002 cabins (with double occupancy) across multiple categories, ranging from interior staterooms and ocean-view cabins to balcony mini-suites and suites.

The accommodation options include the Chairman’s Suite, described as the largest stateroom onboard.

Dining, entertainment and leisure onboard

Cordelia Sky offers a range of dining, entertainment and recreational facilities, including a fitness centre, spa and salon, entertainment shows, casinos, a gaming arcade and the 930-seat Marquee Theatre.

Casino, poker and more

Video arcade, fun gaming for kids and teens

The ship houses approximately 10 restaurants, 11 bars and lounges, a pool deck with two swimming pools and five hot tubs, a sports court, meeting rooms and a library.

Dining options

Spaces such as Palace Restaurant, The Crossings and The Great Outdoor Cafe offer complimentary dining. Meanwhile, speciality dining venues include La Cucina, The Great Sushi Bar, The Local Bar & Grill, Topsiders Bar & Grill, Garden Cafe and Spice Route.

Lounges, bars and shopping

The Chairman’s Club, Connexions and The Dome lounges. The Sky Bar, Atrium Bar and Just Beans offer additional spaces for relaxation.

The ship also features gift shops selling souvenirs, branded merchandise and travel essentials.

Library - the reading lounge

Shows and entertainment

The pool deck and Marquee Theatre serve as venues for large gatherings, celebrations and entertainment programmes. The onboard entertainment schedule includes performances and events such as the skit Tu Aashiqui Hai, the Burlesque! After Midnight party and the Atrium Flashmob.

Domestic cruises from Mumbai

The vessel’s sailing schedule includes several short cruises departing from Mumbai. These include a five-night Goa and Lakshadweep cruise, a four-night Lakshadweep itinerary, a three-night Goa itinerary and a two-night short getaway at sea.

In 2027, Cordelia Sky is also set to offer seven-night Southeast Asian cruises sailing between Chennai and Singapore, with visits to ports in Malaysia and Thailand. The planned destinations include Langkawi, Kuala Lumpur and Phuket.

Cruise fares vary according to the route, duration, sailing period and cabin category.

With the launch of Cordelia Sky, Cordelia Cruises is expanding its fleet and itinerary offerings as it pursues its ambition of making cruising a more widely preferred travel option among Indians.

The vessel previously sailed as Norwegian Sky and Pride of Aloha for Norwegian Cruise Line. Originally built in 1999, the ship has been equipped with updated technology aimed at providing modern comforts.

The company’s Cordelia Empress will now operate from Kochi, its new homeport.

data.title: AU Small Finance Bank Q2 profit jumps 53% to ₹858 cr
data.description:
AU Small Finance Bank on Saturday reported a 53 per cent surge in net profit at ₹858 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026 on the back of improvement in interest income.

The lender had earned a net profit of ₹561 crore in the year-ago period.

Total income rose to ₹6,382 crore in the quarter under review from ₹5,224 crore in the same period a year ago, AU Small Finance Bank said in a regulatory filing.

Interest income increased to ₹5,612 crore as against ₹4,511 crore in the corresponding second quarter of the previous year.

Net interest income of the bank improved to ₹2,820 crore in the July-September quarter, from ₹2,144 crore in the September quarter of 2025, registering a growth of 32 per cent.

Net interest margin increased to 5.8 per cent from 5.5 per cent at the end of September 2025.

Asset quality of the bank also improved with gross non-performing assets (NPAs) rising to 1.99 per cent of gross advances at the end of the September quarter 2026, as against 2.41 per cent a year ago.

Net NPAs or bad loan too moderated to 0.81 per cent, as against 0.88 per cent in the year-ago period.

However, the Capital Adequacy Ratio of the bank decreased to 18.54 per cent, from 18.78 per cent at the end of September 2025.

"This quarter's performance is a reflection of the institution we are steadily building, one that combines growth with profitability, and ambition with prudence," AU Small Finance Bank MD & CEO Sanjay Agarwal said.

The balanced growth of the franchise, improving profitability and stable asset quality reinforce confidence that the foundations for sustained, long-term performance are firmly in place, he added.

data.title: Peter Schiff Says Buy Gold Near $4000 As Prices Sink From January High, Warns Of Currency Crisis Worse Than 2008
data.description:
Key points:
  • Schiff urged investors to buy gold as the metal’s price hovered around nearly $4,000 per ounce on Friday, the lowest since late July.
  • The economist also warned that rising producer prices could further fuel consumer inflation, pointing to September's 1.3% monthly increase in the Producer Price Index.
  • This comes as markets priced in a 68.9% chance of another 25 bps hike in December, according to CME Fed Watch data.

Gold bull Peter Schiff has urged investors to buy gold and silver, given that metals’ slide alongside the U.S. stock market offers a better buying opportunity as inflation picks up again. Schiff warned that current economic factors were “setting up for a crisis” which could be worse than 2008.

“This is an excellent time to buy, as what's bearish for stocks is actually bullish for gold,” Schiff, CEO of Euro Pacific Capital, said in a Friday post on X.

Adding to it, he said silver was also "a great buy below $54."https://x.com/PeterSchiff/status/2113655049666589124?s=20

Gold traded slightly over $4,000 an ounce on Friday, staging a recovery after dipping briefly to around $3,994, its lowest since late July. It subsequently closed at $3,996, down about 1% for the day.

The yellow metal is down about 29% from its record high of $5,608 in January and has lost nearly 7% in the past month. Silver was trading around $61 at the beginning of October.

Warns US Is Heading Toward A Crisis Worse Than 2008

In The Peter Schiff Show Podcast, he cited September wholesale inflation as a red flag for consumers. The Producer Price Index for Final Demand increased 1.3% in September, the largest monthly gain in more than four years, and was 6.3% higher than a year earlier, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported. Much of the climb was driven by energy. The Final Demand Energy Index rose 10.8%.

“What are the producers going to do with these higher prices? They’re going to pass them on,” Schiff added.

According to Schiff, economic growth in the first two years of President Donald Trump's second term was behind President Joe Biden's last two. Commerce Department data showed the economy grew 2.1% in 2025 after 2.8% in 2024 and 2.9% in 2023.

Schiff also said growth slowed to an annualized 1.5% in the second quarter of 2026. The cost of borrowing is still high, he said. According to Freddie Mac’s survey, the average rate on a 30-year fixed mortgage stood at 7.32%, up from 6.19% a year ago. This, he believes, is the reason for the U.S. “setting ourselves up for a crisis” worse than 2008.

“So we are setting ourselves up for a crisis, a financial crisis, a currency crisis, a debt crisis that is much worse than what we had in 2008 and for inflation that’s much higher than we had in 2021,” Schiff said.

Gold’s Biggest Headwind As Markets Price In Another Fed Hike

According to Schiff, this year, rising rates have been gold’s biggest obstacle. Gold doesn’t pay interest, so higher yields make it more costly to hold. The Federal Reserve on Sept. 16 raised its benchmark rate to 3.75%-4%, its first hike since 2023.

Futures markets priced in a 68.9% chance of another 25 bps hike in December as of Saturday, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool, while the odds of a 50 bps hike stood at 7.3%. The Federal Open Market Committee’s (FOMC) next policy meeting is slated for Oct. 27-28.

Why Are Oil Prices Up?

Geopolitical tensions have also put pressure on crude oil prices, which climbed to a six-month high this week following Houthi strikes on Saudi oil infrastructure and reports that the White House is preparing for renewed airstrikes on Iran.

Those gains have added to inflation and rate-hike expectations and have weighed on gold so far rather than lift it, according to Schiff.

data.title: Civil society group raises concerns over composition of expert committee on UCPMP
data.description:
A day after the Centre announced its three-member committee to look into the ethical code on pharmaceutical marketing, the Working Group on Access to Medicines and Treatments has raised concerns about the composition of this expert group.

The group pointed to the inclusion of Dr Naresh Trehan in the expert committee as a potential conflict of interest, given his association with private hospital group Medanta. The group has asked the Department of Pharmaceuticals to recast the committee with a member without a conflict of interest.

As directed by the Supreme Court, the expert committee is to examine the regulatory framework governing pharmaceutical marketing practices and make recommendations on the voluntary Uniform Code for Pharmaceutical Marketing Practices (UCPMP) 2024, a note from the civil society group said, adding, the committee’s mandate is to strengthen ethical practices and promote access to affordable healthcare.

Against that backdrop, it said, “We are concerned that Dr Trehan’s’s inclusion in the committee owing to his financial interests and association with the Medanta Group may give rise to a potential conflict of interest. Given the committee’s mandate it is essential that the deliberations and recommendations remain independent and are guided solely by public health considerations. Our concern is related to the need to safeguard the committee’s independence and impartiality.” A query was sent by businessline to Medanta for Dr Trehan’s view on the issue – a response is awaited.

Pointing to reports in 2018, the group alleged that the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) had examined bills of four hospitals in Delhi / NCR and identified “instances of overcharging, an unethical practice in collaboration with pharmaceutical company, by these hospitals,” they said.

Recent Supreme Court proceedings, as well as evaluations by state drug regulatory authorities in Maharashtra, UP and Karnataka, have also revealed the practice of exorbitant markups in hospital pricing, it added.

“In view of these concerns, we urge the Department of Pharmaceuticals to reconstitute the committee by replacing Dr Trehan with a member who is free of conflict of interest, thereby safeguarding the committee’s integrity and independence.”

While inputs from multiple stakeholders is important, the group said, its concern involves “inclusion of a member whose financial interests give rise to a conflict of interest. It is necessary to ensure that the committee’s recommendations are impartial and transparent, and have a public interest basis.” A possible conflict of interest will undermine the independence of the committee and defeat the very purpose of the Supreme Court’s directions, it added.

data.title: Castrol India Q3 results: Profit drops 49% sequentially as raw material costs weigh on margins
data.description:
Castrol India reported a sequential decline in revenue and profitability for the third quarter, as rising raw material costs and adverse currency movements put pressure on its operating performance.

The company's revenue fell 7.3% quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) to ₹1,734.7 crore from ₹1,871.5 crore in the previous quarter.

Net profit declined 49.3% to ₹176.4 crore from ₹347.7 crore, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) dropped 47% to ₹262.3 crore from ₹494.5 crore.

EBITDA margin contracted to 15.1% from 26.4% in the previous quarter.

Saugata Basuray, managing director of Castrol India, said the company navigated a challenging operating environment during the quarter, marked by a sharp rise in raw material costs and unfavourable currency movements. He said pricing actions implemented earlier in the year helped cushion the impact on margins, while the company continued to invest in expanding its rural distribution network and strengthening its industrial business.

The industrial business recorded another quarter of double-digit volume growth, Basuray said.

Chief Financial Officer Mrinalini Srinivasan said pricing actions taken earlier in the year supported profitability, with EBITDA growing 11% over the first nine months of the calendar year. However, she cautioned that the operating environment was likely to remain volatile and inflationary.

The company will continue to respond to margin pressures through pricing and cost measures, while maintaining its focus on expanding market share across its businesses, Srinivasan said.

Castrol India expands distribution and service network

Castrol India expanded its national distribution footprint to approximately 1.67 lakh outlets, including 46,000 rural outlets, as it continued to strengthen its reach across markets, according to the exchange filing.

Its Auto Care portfolio is now available across around 50,000 physical outlets, in addition to e-commerce and modern trade channels, it said.

The company also expanded its service ecosystem to more than 870 Castrol Auto Service centres, 37,000 independent bike workshops and 16,000 multi-brand workshops. Its Rural Service Express network now covers more than 1,000 locations.

Shares of Castrol India ended 1.39% lower at ₹194.64 on Friday, October 23. The stock has gained 0.6% over the past month and is up 1.8% so far this year.

data.title: Eli Lilly's Next-Generation Ovarian Cancer Drug Shows 79% Response Rate, 100% Disease Control In New Data
data.description:
Key points:
  • Sofe-M is an investigational folate receptor alpha-targeting antibody-drug conjugate, which was evaluated by Lilly with bevacizumab in 33 women with platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer.
  • Among the 29 patients with measurable disease, Lilly stated that the confirmed objective response rate was 79.3%, with 23 patients responding, adding that the disease control rate was 100%.
  • Sofe-M is designed to target FRα on tumor cells and deliver exatecan, a topoisomerase I inhibitor, directly into the cancer cell.

Eli Lilly & Co. (LLY) on Saturday announced new clinical data for its investigational ovarian cancer drug sofetabart mipitecan, or Sofe-M, at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) 2026 Congress in Madrid.

The results come as Lilly continues to test Sofe-M in different types of ovarian cancer, with multiple Phase 3 trials now underway.

Eli Lilly shares closed nearly 3% lower in Friday’s regular trade, but inched up 0.4% during the afterhours session.

Lilly's Ovarian Cancer Drug Shows 79% Response Rate

Sofe-M is an investigational folate receptor alpha (FRα)-targeting antibody-drug conjugate. Lilly evaluated the drug with bevacizumab in 33 women with platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer.

Among the 29 patients with measurable disease, Lilly stated that the confirmed objective response rate was 79.3%, with 23 patients responding, adding that the disease control rate was 100%.

Lilly said responses were consistent across FRα expression levels and regardless of prior poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitor exposure. That is notable given that 67% of patients had previously received a PARP inhibitor and 70% had received bevacizumab.

Patients had received a median of three prior systemic treatment regimens. Median duration of response and median progression-free survival had not been reached at the July 6, 2026 data cutoff, with median follow-ups of 6.2 months and 10.2 months, respectively.

“The durable and robust responses we've seen in patients with platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer are important,” said Chrisann Kyi, MD, a gynecologic medical oncologist and early drug development specialist at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center.

Kyi said the response rate with Sofe-M exceeded what has been reported in published platinum rechallenge studies for patients previously treated with PARP inhibitors.

Lilly Advances Sofe-M Into Phase 3

Sofe-M is designed to target FRα on tumor cells and deliver exatecan, a topoisomerase I inhibitor, directly into the cancer cell. Lilly says the drug is designed to target tumors across a broad range of FRα expression levels.

The company is now evaluating Sofe-M in the three-part Phase 3 FRAmework-01 program.

Part A is testing Sofe-M as a monotherapy in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer. Part B is evaluating Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in platinum-sensitive disease that progressed on or within six months of completing PARP inhibitor treatment. Part C is testing the combination in PARP inhibitor-naïve platinum-sensitive disease.

The Phase 1 safety profile was consistent with the known profiles of the medicines, with no new safety signals reported. The most common treatment-emergent adverse events included epistaxis, nausea, anemia, neutropenia and fatigue.

What Retail Investors Think Of LLY Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Eli Lilly trended in the ‘bearish’ territory at the time of writing.

LLY stock is up 19% year-to-date and 55% over the past 12 months. The S&P 500 ETF (SPY) is up 11% over the past 12 months, while the Vanguard Morningstar Growth ETF (VUG) is up 7%.

data.title: Bihar govt introduces performance assessment index for banks
data.description:
The Bihar government has for the first time introduced a 100-point performance assessment index to rank banks operating in the state, a senior official said on Saturday.

IDFC FIRST Bank currently tops the list with 74 points, Development Commissioner Mihir Kumar Singh said.

“Banks have been classified into three zones based on their score. The Green Zone, indicating excellent performance, includes 11 banks scoring 50 or above, while seven banks fall in the Yellow Zone and several others in the Red Zone. The Red Zone includes leading public sector banks,” a statement issued by the state’s Finance Department said.

Bihar has set an annual credit plan target of ₹4.95 lakh crore for the 2026-27 fiscal. As of September 30, banks disbursed ₹1.89 lakh crore, achieving 38.25 per cent of the target, officials said.

The figure was ₹46,228.29 crore higher than that of the corresponding period last year.

“The Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector recorded 52.68 per cent achievement, with credit disbursement of ₹84,091.21 crore against a target of ₹1.59 lakh crore. Agriculture credit disbursement stood at ₹43,967.17 crore, or 28 per cent of the target,” the release said.

At a high-level review meeting here, Singh directed banks to work in mission mode to achieve their annual credit plan targets, stressing that deposits mobilised in Bihar must be reinvested in the state's development.

Senior officials of the Finance Department, the State Level Bankers' Committee, public and private sector banks, were among those who were part of the meeting.

data.title: Kotak Bank Q2 profit rises 29%, beats estimates
data.description:
Kotak Mahindra Bank
reported a higher-than-expected quarterly ​profit on
Saturday, driven by stronger loan demand ‌and lower provisions
for bad loans.

The country’s ​third-largest private lender by market
capitalisation ⁠posted a stand-alone net profit of ₹4,211 crore ($443.5 million) for the three months ended
September, ‌up from ₹3,253 crore for the same period
last year.

Analysts had ‌expected a profit of ₹4,104 crore,
according ⁠to data compiled by LSEG.

Indian ⁠banks experienced strong loan growth during the
financial second quarter across both corporate and retail
segments, with lending ​against foreign-currency non-resident
deposits ‌also contributing to growth.

In June, the Reserve Bank of India introduced measures,

to attract ‌foreign currency deposits.

Kotak Bank's net interest ​income rose 16 per cent to ₹8,460 crore, aided by a 25 per cent ⁠rise in domestic loans. Deposits grew 23 per cent.

Its net interest margin, a key measure of the ‌bank's

data.title: KEC International bags orders worth ₹2,872 cr from Power Grid Corporation of India

With these wins, the year-to-date order intake has crossed ₹13,500 crore, including ₹9,500 crore from the Transmission and Distribution (T&D) business, the RPG Group company said in a statement.

data.title: Piyush Goyal concludes two-day Germany visit, holds high-level talks to boost trade, investment and technology ties
data.description:
Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal concluded his two-day official visit to Germany, holding a series of high-level meetings in Berlin aimed at strengthening bilateral cooperation in trade, investment, advanced manufacturing, research and emerging technologies, as per a statement by the Ministry of Commerce & Industry.

According to an official statement, Goyal's engagements on October 23 included discussions with senior German government officials, business leaders, research institutions and members of the Indian diaspora, highlighting opportunities to deepen economic and industrial ties between the two countries.

During the visit, Goyal held a bilateral meeting with Levin Holle, Economic and Financial Policy Advisor and G7/G20 Sherpa at the German Federal Chancellery. “The discussions covered bilateral economic cooperation and opportunities to further strengthen economic and investment ties between India and Germany,” the Ministry said.

Goyal also held separate meetings with Siemens Healthineers AG CEO Bernd Montag, Bertelsmann Executive Board Member and Bertelsmann Investments CEO Carsten Coesfeld, and Volkswagen AG CFO and Škoda Auto CEO Holger Peters to explore opportunities for expanding business partnerships, investments and industrial cooperation between India and Germany.

He also participated in a roundtable with leading German industrial research institutions to discuss collaboration in advanced industrial technologies and innovation. “Separately, members of the accompanying Indian business delegation participated in sectoral roundtables with German industry representatives and sectoral associations to explore opportunities for bilateral business collaboration,” the release added.

Apart from this, he also interacted with members of the Indian diaspora in Berlin and addressed the media. Goyal also interacted with Indian science and technology researchers and students based in Germany and held a roundtable with heads of select Fraunhofer Institutes to explore collaboration in microelectronics, power electronics, logistics, smart manufacturing, industrial innovation and battery technologies.

The discussions focused on strengthening research cooperation and industry-academia partnerships between India and Germany. As per government data, India's bilateral trade with Germany stood at $31.03 billion in FY2025-26, with Indian exports to the country registering an 8.44 per cent year-on-year growth compared to FY2024-25, reflecting stronger export performance and sustained bilateral trade ties.

data.title: India's emerging sectors to drive capex, credit demand towards storage, semiconductors: Report
data.description:
Financing demand in India’s emerging sectors is expected to shift towards battery storage, semiconductor packaging, green hydrogen projects with assured buyers and defence suppliers over the next three to five years, as investments in new growth industries create opportunities for banks, according to a Union Bank of India research report.

The report noted artificial intelligence (AI), semiconductors and defence is likely to lead the investment pipeline, with indicative public and private investments of around ₹5.9 lakh crore, ₹5.27 lakh crore and ₹5.07 lakh crore, respectively. It said financing opportunities would increasingly emerge in advanced packaging and assembly of semiconductors, battery recycling, lithium iron phosphate (LFP) and sodium-ion battery capacity, storage infrastructure and component suppliers to the defence industry.

The report also highlighted the potential for financing hydrogen projects backed by assured offtake agreements, while demand for data centres is expected to expand towards edge and colocation facilities as AI inference grows. However, the report cautioned that technology obsolescence, uncertain revenues, delayed payments and long investment payback periods remain significant risks for lenders.

Semiconductor projects typically have payback periods of five to eight years, while space projects may take seven to ten years, exceeding conventional loan tenures, it said. AI infrastructure also faces rapid technology cycles, with graphics processing unit clusters requiring upgrades every 18 to 24 months. The report said ten of the twelve emerging sectors already had identifiable debt-financing routes, while AI and space remained predominantly equity-funded due to technology risks and long payback periods. It recommended that banks develop specialised lending capabilities for semiconductors, hydrogen, data centres and battery storage, alongside products such as milestone-linked disbursements, receivables financing, equipment leasing and green loans.

The report identified renewable energy, semiconductors, green hydrogen and critical minerals as sectors suited to project finance and development finance institution-led funding, while electric vehicles and drones could benefit from asset financing and non-banking financial company lending.

India’s renewable energy capacity stood at 288.6 GW against a target of 500 GW by 2030, while the electric vehicle and battery storage market was projected to grow from $34 billion to $113 billion by 2030. The report said financing opportunities would increasingly move towards commercially viable projects and supply-chain participants as these emerging sectors expand.

data.title: BPCL Q2 profit falls 22% as EBITDA slips on fuel price freeze
data.description:
State-owned Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) reported a 22.5 per cent fall in September quarter net profit as earnings from operations weakened due to a retail price freeze despite rising costs.

BPCL's standalone net profit declined to ₹4,993 crore in July-September, the second quarter of fiscal 2027, from ₹6,443 crore a year earlier, according to a company statement.

Revenue from operations rose to ₹1.58 lakh crore from ₹1.22 lakh crore, while Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortisation (EBITDA) fell nearly 14 per cent to ₹9,437 crore from ₹10,968 crore.

India's second largest fuel retailer earned $32.53 on turning every barrel of crude oil into fuels like petrol and diesel in July-September, as compared to $10.78 a barrel gross refining margin in the same period a year back.

But these gains were wiped away by losses arising from the five month old freeze in retail price revision despite a rise in cost.

BPCL also booked ₹330 crore marketing inventory loss and another ₹397 crore loss due to forex fluctuation.

On a consolidated basis, net profit dropped 21.5 per cent to ₹4,863 crore from ₹6,191 crore, while revenue climbed 29.8 per cent to ₹1.58 lakh crore. Consolidated EBITDA declined 13.4 per cent to ₹9,647 crore.

The divergence between revenue growth and lower earnings highlights the pressure on profitability, even as the firm stepped up investments in refining, gas distribution and alternative fuels.

BPCL reported refinery throughput of 10.41 million tonne in the quarter, operating at 118 per cent of capacity, while domestic market sales stood at 13.47 million tonne. Its refineries had processed 9.82 million tonne of crude oil and sold 12.67 million tonne of fuel in the second quarter of the last fiscal.

The company said it continued investing in infrastructure, supply-chain resilience and digital transformation, while ensuring uninterrupted fuel supplies across the country.

BPCL also has advanced plans for a proposed 10-million-tonne-per-year (MMTPA) greenfield refinery and petrochemical complex at Ramayapatnam in Andhra Pradesh. Its board approved the incorporation of a wholly-owned subsidiary to serve as the dedicated project company, subject to the requisite government, statutory and regulatory approvals.

The proposed complex would expand BPCL's refining and petrochemical footprint, although the announcement did not specify the project's investment outlay or construction timeline.

BPCL also commissioned the Matia LPG bottling plant in Goalpara, Assam, its first such facility in the Northeast, as it seeks to strengthen regional supply infrastructure. The company connected 1.22 lakh new households to Piped Natural Gas (PNG) over the past six months.

On the consumer front, BPCL launched Bharatgas Lite ZIP, a premium LPG offering aimed at improving service convenience, and rolled out more than 9,000 clean, hygienic and odour-free Drive Fresh washrooms across its retail network.

The company continued its 'Zero Ka Dum' programme to improve LPG quality and consumer safety, while expanding its 'Defect Mila Toh Refill Free' initiative, which is now operational in 14 cities.

BPCL said it also stepped up efforts to develop specialised fuels and lower-carbon alternatives. It developed Extreme Weather Grade (XWG) diesel for the Indian Army, designed for military vehicles operating in severe winter conditions and at high altitudes.

In aviation, the company operated a commercial flight using aviation turbine fuel blended with 1 per cent sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), marking a step in its efforts to explore lower-carbon fuel options. The announcement did not disclose the flight's route, the volume of blended fuel used or plans for wider commercial deployment.

Separately, BPCL partnered with Tiki Tar and Shell India Private Limited (TTSIPL) to expand its value-added bitumen portfolio.

BPCL, India's second-largest oil marketing company, operates refineries in Mumbai, Kochi and Bina with combined capacity of about 35.3 million tonne per annum. Its retail network includes more than 25,300 fuel stations and over 6,250 LPG distributorships.

The company has set a target of becoming a net-zero energy company by 2040 for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, which cover direct emissions and those associated with purchased energy, respectively. Its investments in refining, natural gas infrastructure and alternative fuels form part of its broader effort to adapt its business to India's changing energy requirements.

data.title: Adani Wind bags 696 MW orders from five power producers, third-party book crosses 1 GW
data.description:
Adani Wind, the wind energy business of Adani New Industries Ltd, has secured orders totalling 696.2 megawatts (MW) from five power producers, expanding its customer base beyond the Adani Group as India's wind industry shifts towards higher-capacity turbines.

The orders comprise 300 MW from Purvah Green Power, part of the RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group; 155 MW from Jindal India Power, part of the BC Jindal Group; 109.2 MW from NTPC Renewable Energy; 82.5 MW from Aditya Birla Renewables; and 49.5 MW from Integrum Energy, according to people familiar with the matter.

The contracts cover three wind turbine generator platforms rated at 5.2 MW, 5 MW and 3.3 MW, with projects spread across Karnataka, Gujarat and Maharashtra.

With the latest orders, Adani Wind's cumulative order book from independent power producers outside its group has crossed 1 gigawatt (GW), marking a milestone in its efforts to build a third-party business in a market where turbine manufacturers are competing to supply equipment for India's expanding renewable energy capacity, they said.

The largest order, from Purvah Green Power, covers 60 wind turbines rated at 5 MW each for deployment in Bellary, Karnataka. Jindal India Power's 155 MW order comprises 31 turbines of the same rating for installation in Davanagere, Karnataka.

NTPC Renewable Energy has ordered 21 turbines rated at 5.2 MW each for its Khavda project in Gujarat. The Aditya Birla Renewables and Integrum Energy orders will use Adani Wind's 3.3 MW turbine platform for projects in Bhuj, Gujarat and Nandurbar, Maharashtra, respectively, the people said.

The order wins come as Adani Wind seeks to scale up its manufacturing capacity at Mundra, Gujarat, from 2.25 GW annually to 5 GW, with a longer-term target of 10 GW. The expansion would position the company to compete for a larger share of domestic turbine demand and potentially serve overseas markets.

Adani Wind's 5 MW MWL-185 platform has an 185-metre rotor diameter and a 140-metre hub height and is designed for low- to moderate-wind conditions.

Its 5.2 MW MWL-160 platform is among the higher-capacity onshore turbine models listed under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy's Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM).

The company's MWL-160 platform has crossed 2 GW of installations at Khavda, which hosts a large renewable energy development in Gujarat, according to the people. All four of Adani Wind's turbine models are listed under the ministry's approved list, and the company is the only Indian wind turbine manufacturer included in BloombergNEF's global top 15 ranking for 2025.

India, the world's fourth-largest wind power market, has 59.2 GW of installed wind capacity, with a further 43 GW under implementation. The combined base of operational and under-development capacity exceeds 100 GW.

Domestic wind turbine manufacturing capacity has more than doubled from about 12 GW in fiscal 2023 to over 24 GW annually. The industry is targeting installations of around 8 GW in fiscal 2027, with annual additions projected to reach 13.2 GW by fiscal 2031.

India installed a record 6.05 GW of wind capacity in fiscal 2026.

The sector is also moving towards larger turbines and rotor diameters, which can capture more wind energy and improve project economics, depending on local wind conditions, site constraints and infrastructure requirements. Higher-capacity machines can also help developers optimise land use in established wind corridors.

Adani Wind has a portfolio of turbine platforms ranging from 3 MW to 5 MW-plus and is exploring international markets. It has exported blade sets equipped with anti-icing technology to Europe and is engaging with potential customers in the United States, Australia, Brazil and Southeast Asia.

The latest contracts give Adani Wind an opportunity to broaden its customer base as it scales up manufacturing. Securing orders from independent power producers and established energy companies could help demonstrate the commercial acceptance of its technology, although the ultimate contribution to revenue will depend on delivery schedules, project execution and commissioning, analysts said.

data.title: PM Modi to visit Uttar Pradesh and Odisha on October 25
data.description:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Uttar Pradesh and Odisha on Sunday (October 25), where he will inaugurate a garment manufacturing facility in Varanasi, witness the Indian Air Force's aerial display at Namo Ghat and inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India's Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar, according to a press release.

At around 11 am, the Prime Minister will inaugurate Arvind Limited's new garment manufacturing facility in Varanasi, followed by the Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 at Namo Ghat at around 1 pm, where he will attend as the chief guest.

The garment manufacturing facility is expected to strengthen India's textile and apparel manufacturing ecosystem and promote industrial growth in the region, the release stated.

Focusing on modern manufacturing practices, the facility will create employment opportunities, particularly for women, and contribute to the region's economic progress. With a global customer base, it will also enable products manufactured in Varanasi to reach international markets, the release added. The inauguration is expected to highlight Uttar Pradesh's growing role as a destination for industrial investment and manufacturing-led growth, while the predominantly women-led initiative reflects the focus on women-led development.

The Prime Minister will thereafter witness the Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 at Namo Ghat, organised to commemorate the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force under the theme "Wings over Ganges".

The aerial display will feature aircraft, including the Tejas, Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) Prachand, SU-30MKI and Rafale, along with transport aircraft. Aircraft from the Indian Navy and the Indian Army will also participate, showcasing jointness in operations.

The Indian Air Force's premier display teams, including the Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team and the Sarang Helicopter Display Team, will participate in the event, demonstrating precision flying, coordination and operational excellence, according to the release. Thereafter, Modi will travel to Odisha, where he will inaugurate the RBI's Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar at around 4.45 pm and address the gathering.

The newly established facilities are aimed at strengthening the technological foundations of India's financial system by providing a secure, resilient, scalable and future-ready computing ecosystem for the RBI and the broader financial sector, the release stated. Four state-of-the-art data centres will host mission-critical payment and settlement systems, along with other flagship initiatives.

The facility has been certified to the Uptime Institute Tier IV standard, a global benchmark for data centre infrastructure, placing it in the highest tier of operational resilience.

According to the release, the facility is among the largest Tier IV-certified facilities in the Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI) sector worldwide. It is expected to improve the reach, efficiency and reliability of digital financial services and provide a secure digital foundation for India's increasingly technology-driven financial economy.

It will also strengthen the RBI's position in digital infrastructure among central banks. The Cybersecurity Training Institute will provide a dedicated platform for cybersecurity and enterprise-technology training, research and capability development across the sector.

The institute will focus on cutting-edge technologies relevant to the BFSI sector, including quantum computing, artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies, the release added.
